title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — दैवासुरसम्पद्विभागयोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 16: Divine and Demonic Natures
draftNote: Prepared by the Lectorium pipeline from the vulgate text, with a drafting pass, a reviewing pass and a mechanical gate; a printed-edition collation and audio are still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any verse to report a problem.
source: Text: the received (vulgate) text of the Bhagavadgītā, Mahābhārata 6.23–40, as read by Śaṅkara's commentary. Devanagari from Sanskrit Wikisource (भगवद्गीता/दैवासुरसम्पद्विभागयोगः), collated verse by verse against the GRETIL romanized text based on the BORI critical edition (input Tokunaga, rev. J. Smith); every verse where the two differ carries a note giving the BORI reading, and every correction to the Wikisource text is named in its note. Collation against a pre-1930 printed edition is still to be done. Transliteration: IAST. The reading under each word gives the words with sandhi undone and compound members hyphenated, in the manner of the traditional pada-pāṭha. Pronunciation convention: classical Sanskrit as described in Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889); no audio yet. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentary for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.

sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: holy, glorious (honorific prefix)
the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined)
to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

sentences.t:
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः ।
दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥
sentences.tr:
abhayam sattva-saṃśuddhiḥ jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitiḥ |
dānam damaḥ ca yajñaḥ ca svādhyāyaḥ tapaḥ ārjavam ||

morph.gloss: fearlessness (nom. sg. neut., first item of the list of divine qualities that runs through verse 3)
being, one's own nature (first member)
purification, purity (sattva-saṃśuddhi: 'purity of being', nom. sg. fem., list item; -iḥ+j-→-ir j-)
knowledge (first member)
discipline, yoga, kept untranslated per convention (second member)
steadfastness, firm abiding (jñāna-yoga-vyavasthiti: 'steadfastness in the discipline of knowledge', nom. sg. fem., list item)
giving, charity (nom. sg. neut., list item)
self-control, restraint of the senses (nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
and
sacrifice (nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
and
study of one's own [scripture], recitation of the Veda (nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)

austerity (tapaḥ: nom. sg. neut., list item; its own visarga simply drops before the following ā- of ārjavam, with the hiatus retained rather than the vowels fusing to tapārjavam — an accepted option in epic verse, as at 15.16's akṣaraḥ eva)
uprightness, straightforwardness (nom. sg. neut., list item)

sentences.l: Fearlessness, purity-of-being, steadfastness-in-the-yoga-of-knowledge; giving, and self-control, and sacrifice, and study, austerity, uprightness;
sentences.i: Fearlessness, purity of being, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge; giving, self-control, sacrifice, study of scripture, austerity, uprightness;
sentences.n: With no question from Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa continues directly (the speaker line at the head of this verse is generated separately; see conventions.md). Verses 1-3 are a single long asyndetic list of divine qualities — nouns simply set side by side with almost no ca, 'and' — and the sentence's only finite verb, bhavanti, 'they become, they constitute', does not arrive until the end of verse 3. Sandhi: token 2 hides two separate words fused together, sattvasaṃśuddhiḥ + jñānayogavyavasthitiḥ (-iḥ+j-→-ir j-) — 'purity of being' and 'steadfastness in the discipline (yoga, kept untranslated per convention) of knowledge'. In line 2, damaśca and yajñaśca both show -aḥ+c-→-aś c-, a pattern that recurs constantly through this chapter's lists. Svādhyāyastapa āra rjavam is unusual: after svādhyāyaḥ tapaḥ (-aḥ+t-→-as t-), tapaḥ's own visarga simply drops before ārjavam's vowel with the hiatus kept rather than the vowels fusing to tapārjavam — an accepted option in epic verse already seen at 15.16's akṣaraḥ eva.

sentences.t:
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् ।
दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥
sentences.tr:
ahiṃsā satyam akrodhaḥ tyāgaḥ śāntiḥ apaiśunam |
dayā bhūteṣu aloluptvam mārdavam hrīḥ acāpalam ||

morph.gloss: non-violence, non-injury (nom. sg. fem., list item)
truthfulness (nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with akrodhaḥ, -m unaffected before the vowel)
freedom from anger (nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)
renunciation, relinquishment (nom. sg. masc., list item)
tranquility, peace (nom. sg. fem., list item; -iḥ+a-→-ir a-)
freedom from malice, freedom from backbiting (paiśuna, 'slander, calumny'; nom. sg. neut., list item)
compassion (nom. sg. fem., list item; governs bhūteṣu, 'toward beings')
a being, a creature (bhūteṣu: loc. pl., 'toward beings')

freedom from greed, freedom from craving (a-lolupa 'not greedy' + abstract suffix -tva; aloluptvam: nom. sg. neut., list item; -u+a-→-v a-, yaṇ sandhi; with irregular loss of the stem's final -a before the suffix (aloluptvam, not the expected alolupatva) — an archaic/epic formation)
gentleness, softness (nom. sg. neut., list item)
modesty, a sense of shame (hrīḥ: nom. sg. fem., list item; -īḥ+a-→-īr a-)
freedom from fickleness, steadiness (nom. sg. neut., list item)

sentences.l: Non-violence, truthfulness, freedom-from-anger, renunciation, tranquility, and freedom-from-malice; compassion toward-beings, freedom-from-greed, gentleness, modesty, freedom-from-fickleness;
sentences.i: Non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, tranquility, avoidance of malice; compassion for living beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, a sense of shame, steadiness of mind;
sentences.n: The list continues. Token 2, satyam akrodhas tyāgaḥ, hides three separate words (satyam simply joined to akrodhaḥ before the vowel; akrodhaḥ+tyāgaḥ, -aḥ+t-→-as t-). Several items here are themselves privative a- formations, each treated as a single hyphenated lemma (a-krodha, a-paiśuna, a-lolupa-tva, a-cāpala) rather than split into separate morphs, following the pattern already set for such words at 15.5 and 15.7 (a-vyaya, a-mūḍha, a-cetas). Dayā bhūteṣu, 'compassion toward beings', is the one item in the list that governs a case (locative) rather than standing alone.

sentences.t:
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता ।
भवन्ति संपदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥
sentences.tr:
tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucam adrohaḥ na atimānitā |
bhavanti sampadam daivīm abhijātasya bhārata ||

morph.gloss: vigor, fiery energy, brilliance (nom. sg. neut., list item)
patience, forbearance (nom. sg. fem., list item)
fortitude, steadfastness (nom. sg. fem., list item)
cleanliness, purity (nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with adrohaḥ, -m unaffected before the vowel)
freedom from malice, freedom from the wish to injure (nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ before n-→-o)
not (na+atimānitā→nātimānitā, a+a→ā)

excessive pride, arrogance (ati-māna 'excessive pride' + abstract suffix -tā; nātimānitā: 'freedom from excessive pride', nom. sg. fem., list item — note the deliberate contrast with verse 4's darpa, 'pride', among the demonic traits)

to be, become (bhavanti: present 3rd pl., 'they redound to, they constitute'; the verb governing the whole list of verses 1-3 as its subject, and taking sampadam as an accusative of the result reached rather than an ordinary nominative complement — traditionally glossed 'these come to constitute')
endowment, inheritance (acc. sg. fem., the result-accusative object of bhavanti)
divine (fem. adj. of daiva; daivīm: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with sampadam; simply joined with abhijātasya, -m unaffected before the vowel)
born to, born with a natural bent toward (abhijāta: past participle; abhijātasya: gen. sg. masc., 'of one born [with this nature]')
descendant of Bharata, Arjuna (vocative)

sentences.l: Vigor, patience, fortitude, cleanliness, freedom-from-malice, and freedom-from-excessive-pride — these come-to-be the divine endowment of one born [to it], O Bhārata.
sentences.i: vigor, patience, fortitude, cleanliness, freedom from malice, and freedom from excessive pride — these, Bhārata, belong to one born with the divine endowment.
sentences.n: This closes the sentence begun at verse 1: bhavanti, 'they become', governs the whole three-verse list as its subject and takes sampadam daivīm, 'the divine endowment', as an accusative of the result reached rather than an ordinary nominative predicate — the traditional (Śaṅkara) sense is 'these [qualities] redound to, constitute, the divine endowment of one born [with such a nature]', abhijātasya being a genitive agreeing with an understood 'person'. Nātimānitā, 'freedom from excessive pride' (na+atimānitā, a+a→ā), closes the divine list on a quality that verse 4's darpa, 'pride', will directly oppose in the demonic list — one of several such deliberate echoes between the two catalogs, though the catalogs themselves are of very unequal length (some 26 items across three verses against six in one). Bhārata is Arjuna, descendant of Bharata, addressed here for the first time in the chapter.

sentences.t:
दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च ।
अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ संपदमासुरीम् ॥
sentences.tr:
dambhaḥ darpaḥ abhimānaḥ ca krodhaḥ pāruṣyam eva ca |
ajñānam ca abhijātasya pārtha sampadam āsurīm ||

morph.gloss: hypocrisy, deceit, ostentation (nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ before d-→-o)
pride, insolence, arrogance (nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
self-conceit, excessive self-regard (nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
and (BORI reads darpo 'timānaś ca here — atimāna, 'excessive pride' — in place of the vulgate's darpo 'bhimānaś ca, abhimāna 'self-conceit'; see the note)
anger (nom. sg. masc., list item)
harshness, roughness (nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with eva, -m unaffected before the vowel)
indeed, even, alone
and
ignorance (nom. sg. neut., list item)
and (ca+abhijātasya→cābhijātasya, a+a→ā)
born to (abhijāta: past participle; abhijātasya: gen. sg. masc., 'of one born [with this nature]', as at verse 3)
son of Pṛthā, Arjuna (vocative)
endowment, inheritance (sampadam: acc. sg. fem., result-accusative object, as at verse 3; simply joined with āsurīm)
demonic (fem. adj. of āsura; āsurīm: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with sampadam)

sentences.l: Hypocrisy, pride, and self-conceit, anger, harshness, and also ignorance — these [come to be] the demonic endowment of one born [to it], O Pārtha.
sentences.i: Hypocrisy, pride and self-conceit, anger, harshness, and ignorance — these, Pārtha, belong to one born with the demonic endowment.
sentences.n: The mirror-list of vices, built exactly like verses 1-3 (bhavanti and sampadam are understood, carried over from verse 3 rather than repeated). darpo 'bhimānaś ca hides two words, darpaḥ (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha) and abhimānaḥ ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-): darpa is 'pride, insolence', abhimāna 'self-conceit, an inflated opinion of oneself'. This is one of the chapter's two places where the received (vulgate) text differs from the BORI critical edition: BORI reads darpo 'timānaś ca, 'pride and excessive pride (atimāna)', in place of the vulgate's darpo 'bhimānaś ca, 'pride and self-conceit (abhimāna)' printed here. Pārtha, 'son of Pṛthā', is again Arjuna.

sentences.t:
दैवी संपद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता ।
मा शुचः संपदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥
sentences.tr:
daivī sampat vimokṣāya nibandhāya āsurī matā |
mā śucaḥ sampadam daivīm abhijātaḥ asi pāṇḍava ||

morph.gloss: divine (fem. adj., nom. sg., subject)
endowment, inheritance (sampat: nom. sg. fem., subject; sampat+vimokṣāya→sampad vimokṣāya, -t+v-→-d v-, a stop voiced before the following voiced consonant)
liberation, release (vimokṣāya: dat. sg., 'for liberation', purpose)
bondage (nibandhāya: dat. sg., 'for bondage', purpose, paired with vimokṣāya)
demonic (fem. adj., nom. sg., subject, second of the pair; nibandhāya+āsurī→nibandhāyāsurī, a+ā→ā)
thought, held to be, considered (mata: past participle of man; matā: nom. sg. fem., predicate, agreeing with both daivī and āsurī of this verse)
do not (prohibitive particle, taking the following injunctive)
to grieve (śucaḥ: injunctive 2nd sg. with mā, 'do not grieve')
endowment, inheritance (acc. sg. fem., object of abhijātaḥ, the participle, 'born to'; as at verses 3-4's abhijāta-/abhijātasya + sampadam)
divine (daivīm: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with sampadam; simply joined with abhijātaḥ)
born to (abhijāta: past participle; abhijātaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate agreeing with 'you'; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
to be (asi: present 2nd sg., 'you are')
son of Pāṇḍu, Arjuna (vocative)

sentences.l: The divine endowment [is] held [to lead] to liberation, the demonic to bondage; do not grieve, you are born, O Pāṇḍava, to the divine endowment.
sentences.i: The divine endowment, it is held, leads to liberation; the demonic, to bondage. Do not grieve, Pāṇḍava — you were born with the divine endowment.
sentences.n: A single balanced sentence names the stakes of the whole chapter: daivī sampat vimokṣāya, 'the divine endowment [is] for liberation', āsurī nibandhāya, 'the demonic, for bondage' (matā, 'held to be', agreeing with both), the two datives of purpose (vimokṣāya, nibandhāya) set side by side. The second line turns personal: mā śucaḥ, 'do not grieve' (a prohibitive mā with the injunctive śucaḥ, the same construction already used at 18.66's mā śucaḥ; 2.11's aśocyān anvaśocas tvam shares the root √śuc but is a different, ordinary indicative construction, not this prohibitive), reassures Arjuna directly that he himself, daivīm sampadam abhijātaḥ asi, 'you are born to the divine endowment' — answering, in effect, his own despair from chapter 1. Pāṇḍava, 'son of Pāṇḍu', is again Arjuna.

sentences.t:
द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च ।
दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु ॥
sentences.tr:
dvau bhūta-sargau loke asmin daivaḥ āsuraḥ eva ca |
daivaḥ vistaraśaḥ proktaḥ āsuram pārtha me śṛṇu ||

morph.gloss: two (dvau: nom. dual masc.)
a being, a creature (first member)
creation, class, order (bhūta-sarga: 'classes of created beings', nom. dual masc., subject)
world (loke: loc. sg.; loke+asmin→loke'smin, e+a→e with the a- elided, marked by avagraha)
this (asmin: loc. sg. masc., 'in this')

divine (daivaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, first of the pair; asmin+daivaḥ simply joined, the dental nasal unaffected before the following dental d-; daivaḥ's own visarga then drops before the following āsuraḥ, hiatus kept rather than coalescing — the same accepted epic option flagged for āsuraḥ eva immediately below, and already seen at 15.16's akṣaraḥ eva.)
demonic (nom. sg. masc., predicate, second of the pair; -aḥ+e-→-a e-, hiatus retained rather than fusing to -aiva, as at 15.16's akṣaraḥ eva — an accepted option in epic verse)
indeed, even, alone
and
the divine [kind] (nom. sg. masc., subject, resuming 6a's daivaḥ; -aḥ before v-→-o)
extension, fullness, detail (vistaraśaḥ: adverb, 'at length, in detail', formed with the adverbial suffix -śas)
declared, described (prokta: past participle; proktaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate agreeing with daivaḥ, 'has been described'; final -ḥ dropped before the following vowel a-, hiatus retained as at 6a)
the demonic [kind] (acc. sg. masc., object of śṛṇu, resuming bhūtasargau)
Arjuna (vocative)
I (me: enclitic gen./abl. sg., 'from me')
to hear (śṛṇu: imperative 2nd sg., 'hear!')

sentences.l: Two [are] the creations-of-beings in this world, the divine and the demonic too; the divine has been described at-length — hear from me, O Pārtha, of the demonic.
sentences.i: There are two kinds of created beings in this world, the divine and the demonic. I have described the divine at length; now hear from me, Pārtha, about the demonic.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's long central section (through verse 20) on the demonic nature. Bhūta-sargau, 'the two creations/classes of beings', is dual, matching dvau, 'two'. The line hides two separate hiatuses, both left unfused rather than coalescing, in the manner already noted at 15.16's akṣaraḥ eva: loke'smin (loke+asmin, e+a, the a- elided and marked by avagraha) daiva āsura eva ca — daivaḥ loses its visarga before āsuraḥ with the vowels kept apart rather than fusing, and āsuraḥ likewise loses its visarga before eva rather than fusing to āsuraiva. Note that 'the divine has already been described at length' (prokta) refers to nothing earlier in the poem by that name; it is simply Kṛṣṇa's own summary of the divine list just given in verses 1-3, now signaling a matching, and much longer, catalog of the demonic to follow.

sentences.t:
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः ।
न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
pravṛttim ca nivṛttim ca janāḥ na viduḥ āsurāḥ |
na śaucam na api ca ācāraḥ na satyam teṣu vidyate ||

morph.gloss: right action, engagement, activity (acc. sg. fem., object of viduḥ)
and
cessation, withdrawal from action (acc. sg. fem., object of viduḥ)
and
a person, people (janāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; -āḥ before n-→-ā)
not
to know (viduḥ: perfect 3rd pl. used as present, 'they know'; -uḥ+ā-→-ur ā-, the visarga after u becoming r before a voiced sound)
demonic (āsurāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject, in apposition with janāḥ, 'demonic people')
not
purity, cleanliness (nom. sg. neut., subject)
not (na+api→nāpi, a+a→ā)
also, even
and (ca+ācāraḥ→cācāraḥ, a+ā→ā)
right conduct, proper behavior (ācāraḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before n-→-o)
not
truth, truthfulness (nom. sg. neut., subject)
in them (teṣu: loc. pl. masc., referring to the āsurāḥ of the first line)
to exist, be found (vidyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is found')

sentences.l: Right-action and its-cessation, demonic people do not know; nor purity, nor also right-conduct, nor truth is found in them.
sentences.i: Demonic people know neither right action nor its cessation; they have no purity, no right conduct, no truthfulness.
sentences.n: Pravṛtti and nivṛtti, 'engagement in action' and 'withdrawal from action', are a standing technical pair in the poem (the same terms return, e.g., at 18.30's own pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca) naming the two poles of moral life: knowing when to act and when not to. Vidur āsurāḥ (viduḥ+āsurāḥ, the visarga after u becoming r before a voiced sound) puts āsurāḥ, 'demonic [people]', in apposition with janāḥ, 'people' — this is the first verse to actually name who is being described, opening a run of purely negative description (verses 7-8 deny them everything) that will run through to the men's own words in verses 13-15.

sentences.t:
असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् ।
अपरस्परसंभूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम् ॥
sentences.tr:
asatyam apratiṣṭham te jagat āhuḥ anīśvaram |
aparaspara-saṃbhūtam kim anyat kāma-haitukam ||

morph.gloss: unreal, untrue (asatyam: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with jagat, first predicate; simply joined with apratiṣṭham)
without foundation, groundless (apratiṣṭham: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with jagat, second predicate)
they (te: nom. pl. masc., subject, referring to the āsurāḥ of verse 7)
the world (acc. sg. neut., object of āhuḥ; jagat+āhuḥ→jagadāhuḥ, -t+ā-→-d ā-, a stop voiced before a vowel)
to say, declare (āhuḥ: perfect 3rd pl., 'they say'; -uḥ+a-→-ur a-, the visarga after u becoming r before a voiced sound)
without a lord, without a god, godless (anīśvaram: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with jagat, third predicate)
one another, mutual(ly) (an old form synonymous with the more familiar paraspara, so glossed already by Śaṅkara — not the privative a- 'not', which would reverse the sense; first member)
produced, arisen (saṃbhūta: past participle; aparaspara-saṃbhūtam: 'produced by mutual union', acc. sg. neut., predicate agreeing with jagat)
what? (interrogative, 'what else [could it be]')
other, else (nom./acc. sg. neut.)
desire (first member)
caused by, having as its cause (from hetu, 'cause'; kāma-haitukam: 'caused by desire alone', acc. sg. neut., predicate)

sentences.l: Unreal, without-foundation, they say the world [is], without-a-god; produced-by-mutual-union, [with] desire-as-its-only-cause — what else?
sentences.i: They say the world is unreal, baseless, without a god, produced by mere mutual union, with desire as its only cause — what else could it be?
sentences.n: This states the demonic cosmology the chapter condemns, directly opposed to the theistic vision of chapters 9-11: the world (jagat) is asatyam, 'unreal', apratiṣṭham, 'without foundation', anīśvaram, 'without a lord, godless'. Aparasparasaṃbhūtam is a well-known crux: aparaspara here is not the privative a- 'not' plus paraspara 'mutual' (which would reverse the sense to 'not produced by mutual [causation]'), but an old form used, already by Śaṅkara's own gloss, as a simple synonym of paraspara, 'one another' — so 'produced by mutual union [of male and female]', with no higher cause. The rhetorical question kim anyat kāma-haitukam, 'what else, caused by desire?', closes the verse: for the demonic view, desire alone explains everything.

sentences.t:
एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः ।
प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥
sentences.tr:
etām dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya naṣṭa-ātmānaḥ alpa-buddhayaḥ |
prabhavanti ugra-karmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagataḥ ahitāḥ ||

morph.gloss: this (etām: acc. sg. fem., object of avaṣṭabhya, 'this view')
a view, an opinion, an outlook (acc. sg. fem., object of avaṣṭabhya; simply joined with avaṣṭabhya)
to hold fast to, cling to, adopt (avaṣṭabhya: gerund, 'having taken hold of')
lost, ruined (past participle of naś; first member)
self (naṣṭa-ātman: 'whose self is lost', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
little, small (first member)
intelligence, understanding (alpa-buddhi: 'of little intelligence', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., in apposition)
to arise, come forth (prabhavanti: present 3rd pl., 'they arise'; -i+u-→-y u-)
fierce, terrible (first member)
deed, action (ugra-karman: 'of fierce deeds', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., in apposition)
destruction, ruin (dat. sg., purpose; jagataḥ below serves both kṣayāya and ahitāḥ, 'for the destruction of the world' and 'enemies of the world')
world (jagataḥ: gen. sg.; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
hostile, harmful (ahitāḥ: nom. pl. masc., predicate, 'as enemies')

sentences.l: Holding-fast-to this view, their-selves-lost, of-little-intelligence, they arise, of-fierce-deeds, for the destruction of the world, as-its-enemies.
sentences.i: Clinging to this view, their true selves lost, of little understanding, they arise, men of cruel deeds, as enemies of the world, bent on its destruction.
sentences.n: Etāṃ dṛṣṭim, 'this view', points back to verse 8's nihilistic cosmology. Two bahuvrīhi compounds describe the men holding it: naṣṭātmānaḥ, 'whose [true] selves are lost' (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha), and alpa-buddhayaḥ, 'of little intelligence'; a third, ugra-karmāṇaḥ, 'of fierce deeds', describes how they act. The clause kṣayāya jagato 'hitāḥ shares one genitive, jagataḥ, between two constructions — 'for the destruction of the world' and 'as enemies of the world' — a common economy in Sanskrit where a single case-form serves two phrases at once.

sentences.t:
काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः ।
मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः ॥
sentences.tr:
kāmam āśritya duṣpūram dambha-māna-mada-anvitāḥ |
mohāt gṛhītvā asat-grāhān pravartante aśuci-vratāḥ ||

morph.gloss: desire (acc. sg. masc., object of āśritya; simply joined with āśritya)
to resort to, give oneself over to (āśritya: gerund, 'having given themselves over to')
hard to fill, insatiable (duṣ- 'ill, hard' + pūra 'filling'; acc. sg. masc., agreeing with kāmam)
hypocrisy, deceit, ostentation (first member)
pride, self-conceit (second member)
arrogance (third member)
possessed by, filled with (from anu-i; dambha-māna-mada-anvitāḥ: 'filled with hypocrisy, pride and arrogance', nom. pl. masc., subject)
delusion (mohāt: abl. sg., 'through delusion'; mohāt+gṛhītvā→mohādgṛhītvā, -t+g-→-d g-)
to seize, adopt (gṛhītvā: gerund, 'having adopted'; gṛhītvā+asadgrāhān→gṛhītvāsadgrāhān, ā+a→ā)
untrue, false (first member)
a notion, a tenet, a holding (asat-grāha: 'false notions', acc. pl. masc., object of gṛhītvā; -t+g-→-d g-)
to proceed, act (pravartante: present middle 3rd pl., 'they act'; grāhān+pravartante simply joined, the final -n unaffected before p-)
impure (first member)

a vow, a resolve, an observance (aśuci-vratāḥ: 'whose resolves are impure', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject; pravartante+aśucivratāḥ→pravartante'śucivratāḥ, -e+a-→-e' with avagraha) — the densest single-token sandhi run in this chapter: the whole second half-line is one written token

sentences.l: Given-over-to insatiable desire, filled-with-hypocrisy-pride-and-arrogance, through delusion holding-to false-notions, they act, their-observances-impure.
sentences.i: Given over to desire that can never be satisfied, filled with hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, clinging through delusion to false notions, they act with their resolves impure.
sentences.n: The whole second half-line of this verse — mohād gṛhītvāsadgrāhān pravartante 'śucivratāḥ — is written as a single unbroken Devanagari token, the densest sandhi run in the chapter; reading it means finding five separate words inside it: mohāt (abl., 'through delusion'; -t+g-→-d g-), gṛhītvā ('having adopted'; +a-→ā, vowel fusion), asad-grāhān ('false notions', -t+g-→-d g-, acc. pl., object of gṛhītvā), pravartante ('they act'), and aśuci-vratāḥ ('whose observances are impure', -e+a-→-e' with avagraha). Kāmam duṣpūram āśritya, 'given over to desire hard to fill/insatiable', and dambha-māna-mada-anvitāḥ, 'filled with hypocrisy, pride and arrogance', complete the first line's description.

sentences.t:
चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः ।
कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः ॥
sentences.tr:
cintām aparimeyām ca pralaya-antām upāśritāḥ |
kāma-upabhoga-paramāḥ etāvat iti niścitāḥ ||

morph.gloss: anxiety, care, worry (acc. sg. fem., object of upāśritāḥ; simply joined with aparimeyām)
immeasurable, unlimited (aparimeyām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with cintām)
and
dissolution, death (first member; pralaya+antām→pralayāntām, a+a→ā)
end (pralaya-antām: 'ending [only] in death', acc. sg. fem., agreeing with cintām; simply joined with upāśritāḥ)
beset by, given over to (upāśrita: past participle; upāśritāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject)
desire (first member)
enjoyment (second member; kāma+upabhoga→kāmopabhoga, a+u→o)

highest, supreme (kāma-upabhoga-paramāḥ: 'holding sense-enjoyment as the highest goal', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject; its own -āḥ drops before the following vowel of etāvat, as elsewhere in this chapter wherever a plural in -āḥ meets a voiced sound.)
this much, so much (nom. sg. neut., 'this is all [there is]')
thus, [thinking] (quotation particle marking the preceding as a thought; etāvat+iti→etāvaditi, -t+i-→-d i-, a stop voiced before a vowel)
determined, certain, resolved (niścita: past participle; niścitāḥ: nom. pl. masc., predicate agreeing with the subject)

sentences.l: Beset-by immeasurable anxiety, ending-only-in-death, holding-sense-enjoyment-as-the-highest-goal, certain [that] 'this-much [is all],'
sentences.i: Beset by anxiety beyond measure, ending only in death, holding sense-enjoyment as life's highest goal, sure that this is all there is —
sentences.n: This verse continues the sentence into verse 12 (there is no finite verb here; īhante, 'they strive', in verse 12 carries the whole description). Cintām aparimeyāṃ pralayāntām upāśritāḥ, 'beset by immeasurable anxiety ending [only] in death' (pralaya-antām, 'having death as its end'), and kāmopabhogaparamāḥ, 'holding the gratification of desire as the highest [goal]' (bahuvrīhi), lead into a quoted thought marked by iti: etāvad iti niścitāḥ, 'certain that "this is all [there is]"' — the first of several places in this section where the demonic men's own reasoning is quoted directly, anticipating the extended monologue of verses 13-15.

sentences.t:
आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः ।
ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् ॥
sentences.tr:
āśā-pāśa-śataiḥ baddhāḥ kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ |
īhante kāma-bhoga-artham anyāyena artha-sañcayān ||

morph.gloss: hope, expectation (first member)
a tie, a bond, a snare (second member; āśā+pāśa→āśāpāśa)
a hundred (āśā-pāśa-śataiḥ: 'by hundreds of ties of hope', instr. pl.; -aiḥ+b-→-air b-)
bound, tied (baddha: past participle; baddhāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject, 'bound')
desire (first member)
anger (second member)
intent on, given over to (kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ: 'given over to desire and anger', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., in apposition)
to strive, endeavor (īhante: present middle 3rd pl., 'they strive')
desire (first member)
enjoyment (second member; kāma+bhoga→kāmabhoga)
purpose, sake (kāma-bhoga-artham: 'for the sake of gratifying desire', adverbial acc.; simply joined with anyāyena)
injustice, wrong means (anyāyena: instr. sg., 'by unjust means'; anyāyena+arthasañcayān→anyāyenārthasañcayān, a+a→ā)
wealth, riches (first member)
accumulation, amassing (artha-sañcayān: 'hoards of wealth', acc. pl. masc., object of īhante)

sentences.l: Bound by hundreds-of-ties-of-hope, given-over-to desire-and-anger, they strive, for-the-sake-of-gratifying-desire, by unjust-means, [to amass] hoards-of-wealth.
sentences.i: Bound by hundreds of chains of hope, given over to desire and anger, they strive by unjust means to amass wealth for the sake of gratifying their desires.
sentences.n: Āśā-pāśa-śataiḥ baddhāḥ, 'bound by hundreds of ties of hope' (āśā, 'hope, expectation', pictured as a rope binding them), and kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ, 'given over to desire and anger' (a phrase that will recur, in the singular, at verse 21's naming of desire and anger among the three gates of hell), set up the verse's one finite verb, īhante, 'they strive'. The final compound, kāma-bhoga-artham anyāyena artha-sañcayān, 'for the sake of gratifying desire, by unjust means, hoards of wealth', packs the whole point of their striving into a single phrase: acquisition, by any means, for the sake of appetite.

sentences.t:
इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् ।
इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥
sentences.tr:
idam adya mayā labdham imam prāpsye manoratham |
idam asti idam api me bhaviṣyati punaḥ dhanam ||

morph.gloss: this (nom./acc. sg. neut., understood object, 'this [much]')
today, now (adverb)
I (mayā: instr. sg., 'by me')
obtained, gained (labdha: past participle; labdham: nom. sg. neut., predicate, 'this has been gained')
this (imam: acc. sg. masc., object of prāpsye, vulgate reading agreeing with manoratham, masc.; BORI reads idam, neuter, in its place — see the note)
to reach, attain, obtain (prāpsye: future middle 1st sg., 'I shall gain')
mind (first member)
chariot; manoratha 'mind's chariot', i.e. a wish, a desire (acc. sg. masc., object of prāpsye)
this (nom. sg. neut., subject, 'this is [mine]')
to be (asti: present 3rd sg., 'is'; asti+idam→astīdam, i+i→ī)
this (nom. sg. neut., subject, second clause; simply joined with api)
also, too
I (me: enclitic gen. sg., 'my')
to be, become (bhaviṣyati: future 3rd sg., 'will be')
again, further (punar: adverb; the basic form of this word before voiced sounds, with punaḥ its pausa form; punaḥ+dhanam→punardhanam)
wealth (nom. sg. neut., subject, 'this wealth too [shall be mine]')

sentences.l: 'This today by-me has-been-gained; this desire I-shall-attain [next]; this exists, and this wealth too shall further be mine.'
sentences.i: 'This I have gained today; this desire I shall fulfill next. This is mine, and this wealth too will be mine besides.'
sentences.n: Verses 13-15 quote the demonic man's inner monologue directly, closed by iti at the end of verse 15 (modiṣya iti) — grammatically all of it is what he is imagined saying to himself. This is the second of the chapter's two places where the vulgate differs from BORI: the vulgate reads labdham imaṃ prāpsye, 'this [imam, masculine, agreeing with manoratham] I shall attain', which is what is printed and read here; BORI reads labdham idaṃ prāpsye, with the neuter idam in its place. Manoratham, literally 'mind's chariot', is the ordinary Sanskrit word for 'a wish, a fancy, a desire' — the thing this man is forever chasing next.

sentences.t:
असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि ।
ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी ॥
sentences.tr:
asau mayā hataḥ śatruḥ haniṣye ca aparān api |
īśvaraḥ aham aham bhogī siddhaḥ aham balavān sukhī ||

morph.gloss: that (asau: nom. sg. masc., subject, 'that [enemy]')
I (mayā: instr. sg., 'by me')
slain (hata: past participle; hataḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, 'has been slain')
enemy (śatruḥ: nom. sg. masc., in apposition with asau; -uḥ+h-→-ur h-)
to slay (haniṣye: future middle 1st sg., 'I shall slay')
and (ca+aparān→cāparān, a+a→ā)
other (aparān: acc. pl. masc., object of haniṣye; simply joined with api)
also, too
lord, master, ruler (nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
I (nom. sg., subject, 'I am the lord')
I (nom. sg., subject, repeated for the next clause; simply joined with bhogī)
enjoyer, one who enjoys (nom. sg. masc., predicate, 'I am the enjoyer')
accomplished, perfected (siddha: past participle; siddhaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
I (nom. sg., subject, repeated a third time)
powerful, strong (balavān: nom. sg. masc., predicate)
happy (nom. sg. masc., predicate)

sentences.l: 'That enemy has-been-slain by-me, and I-shall-slay others too; I [am] the lord, I [am] the enjoyer, I [am] accomplished, powerful, happy;'
sentences.i: 'That enemy I have killed, and I will kill others too. I am the lord, I am the one who enjoys, I am accomplished, powerful, and happy.'
sentences.n: The monologue continues with a string of first-person boasts, aham repeated three times — once eliding into īśvaraḥ (īśvaro'ham, -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha), immediately doubled before bhogī (aham aham, the second simply following the first, -m unaffected before the vowel), and once more eliding into siddhaḥ (siddho'ham, -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha): 'I am the lord [īśvaraḥ], I am the enjoyer [bhogī], I am accomplished [siddhaḥ], powerful, happy.' The self-glorifying anaphora is the point — each clause restates the same swollen 'I' in a new guise, exactly the ahaṃkāra, 'egotism', that verse 18 will name outright.

sentences.t:
आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया ।
यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥
sentences.tr:
āḍhyaḥ abhijanavān asmi kaḥ anyaḥ asti sadṛśaḥ mayā |
yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣye iti ajñāna-vimohitāḥ ||

morph.gloss: wealthy, rich (nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
well-born, of good lineage (abhijanavān: nom. sg. masc., predicate; simply joined with asmi)
to be (asmi: present 1st sg., 'I am')
who? (kaḥ: nom. sg. masc. interrogative; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
other, else (anyaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
to be, to exist (asti: present 3rd sg., 'is there')
like, equal to (sadṛśaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate agreeing with anyaḥ; -aḥ before m-→-o)
I (mayā: instr. sg. of comparison, 'with me, to me')
to sacrifice (yakṣye: future middle 1st sg., 'I shall sacrifice' — the ātmanepada 'for oneself' form)
to give (dāsyāmi: future 1st sg., 'I shall give')

to rejoice (modiṣye: future middle 1st sg., 'I shall rejoice'; before the following iti its ātmanepada -e ending drops to -a rather than the usual hiatus or coalescence — an idiosyncratic sandhi of this ending before iti, attested here in the transmitted text: modiṣye+iti→modiṣya iti)
thus, [so they think] (quotation particle, closing the interior monologue begun at verse 13; iti+ajñāna→ityajñāna, -i+a-→-y a-)
ignorance (first member)
deluded (vimohita: past participle, causative; vimohitāḥ: nom. pl. masc., predicate, the narrator's own judgment on the men just quoted)

sentences.l: 'I [am] wealthy and well-born; who else is there like me? I-shall-sacrifice, I-shall-give, I-shall-rejoice' — thus, deluded-by-ignorance,
sentences.i: 'I am rich and well-born — who else is there like me? I shall sacrifice, I shall give gifts, I shall enjoy myself' — so they think, deluded by ignorance,
sentences.n: The monologue closes here, marked by iti: modiṣya iti, 'thus [thinking], "I shall rejoice."' Modiṣye, the plain future middle 'I shall rejoice', shows an idiosyncratic sandhi before this particular iti, its ātmanepada -e ending simply becoming -a (modiṣye+iti→modiṣya iti) rather than the usual coalescence or retained hiatus seen elsewhere in the chapter — an oddity of this verb-ending before iti, reproduced here exactly as transmitted. Ajñāna-vimohitāḥ, 'deluded by ignorance', is the narrator's own verdict, stepping back from the quoted boast to name it for what it is, and opening directly into verse 16's account of where such delusion leads.

sentences.t:
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः ।
प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥
sentences.tr:
aneka-citta-vibhrāntāḥ moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ |
prasaktāḥ kāma-bhogeṣu patanti narake aśucau ||

morph.gloss: not one, manifold, many (first member)
thought, mind (second member; aneka+citta→anekacitta)
bewildered, distracted (vibhrānta: past participle; aneka-citta-vibhrāntāḥ: 'bewildered by manifold thoughts', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject)
delusion (first member)
a net, a web (moha-jāla: 'the net of delusion', second member)
enveloped, entangled (samāvṛta: past participle; moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ: 'entangled in the net of delusion', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., in apposition)
attached to, addicted to (prasakta: past participle; prasaktāḥ: nom. pl. masc., predicate)
desire (first member)
enjoyment (kāma-bhogeṣu: 'in the gratification of desire', loc. pl.)
to fall (patanti: present 3rd pl., 'they fall')
hell (loc. sg., 'into hell')
foul, impure (aśucau: loc. sg., agreeing with narake; -e+a-→-e' with avagraha)

sentences.l: Bewildered-by-manifold-thoughts, entangled-in-the-net-of-delusion, addicted to the gratification-of-desire, they fall into a foul hell.
sentences.i: Confused by countless thoughts, caught in the net of delusion, addicted to sense-gratification, they fall into a foul hell.
sentences.n: Two bahuvrīhi compounds describe the fate of the men whose monologue just closed: aneka-citta-vibhrāntāḥ, 'bewildered by manifold (an-eka, 'not-one') thoughts', and moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ, 'entangled in the net of delusion'. Prasaktāḥ kāma-bhogeṣu, 'addicted to the gratification of desire', gives the one finite verb of the verse, patanti, its subject: they fall, patanti, narake 'śucau, 'into a foul hell' (-e+a-→-e' with avagraha) — the first of two consequences (this and verse 19-20's rebirth in demonic wombs) that the chapter draws from the character just described.

sentences.t:
आत्मसंभाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः ।
यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
sentences.tr:
ātma-saṃbhāvitāḥ stabdhāḥ dhana-māna-mada-anvitāḥ |
yajante nāma-yajñaiḥ te dambhena avidhi-pūrvakam ||

morph.gloss: self (first member)
esteemed, self-conceited (causative saṃbhāvita, 'considered, esteemed'; ātma-saṃbhāvitāḥ: 'self-conceited', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject)

stiff, obstinate, arrogant (stabdha: past participle; stabdhāḥ: nom. pl. masc., in apposition; the visarga of -āḥ drops before the following voiced dh- of dhanamānamadānvitāḥ, as elsewhere in this chapter wherever a plural in -āḥ meets a voiced sound)
wealth (first member)
pride, self-conceit (second member)
arrogance (third member; dhana+māna+mada→dhanamānamada)
filled with, possessed by (dhana-māna-mada-anvitāḥ: 'filled with the pride and arrogance of wealth', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., in apposition; dhanamānamada+anvitāḥ→dhanamānamadānvitāḥ, a+a→ā)
to sacrifice (yajante: present middle 3rd pl., 'they sacrifice')
name (first member)
sacrifice (nāma-yajñaiḥ: 'with sacrifices that are such in name only', instr. pl.)
they (te: nom. pl. masc., subject, resuming verse 17a; -aiḥ+t-→-ais t-)
hypocrisy, deceit, ostentation (dambhena: instr. sg., 'with hypocrisy'; dambhena+avidhi→dambhenāvidhi, a+a→ā)
not according to rule, improper (first member)
preceded by, characterized by (avidhi-pūrvakam: 'not according to proper rule', adverbial acc.)

sentences.l: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled-with-the-pride-and-arrogance-of-wealth, they sacrifice, with-sacrifices-in-name-only, with hypocrisy, not-according-to-rule.
sentences.i: Self-important and stubborn, puffed up with the pride of wealth, they perform sacrifices that are sacrifices in name only, out of hypocrisy, without regard for the proper rites.
sentences.n: A new group of demonic traits, centered on false religion: ātma-saṃbhāvitāḥ, 'self-esteeming, self-conceited', and stabdhāḥ, 'stubborn, arrogant' (its visarga dropping before the voiced dh- that follows, as elsewhere in this chapter's -āḥ endings), dhana-māna-mada-anvitāḥ, 'filled with the pride and arrogance of wealth'. Such men yajante nāma-yajñais, 'sacrifice with name-sacrifices' — rites that are sacrifices in name only — dambhena avidhi-pūrvakam, 'with hypocrisy, not according to [scriptural] rule (vidhi)' — the word vidhi returning at the chapter's very end, in verse 24's śāstra-vidhi, 'the injunction of scripture', which these men flout in advance.

sentences.t:
अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः ।
मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः ॥
sentences.tr:
ahaṃkāram balam darpam kāmam krodham ca saṃśritāḥ |
mām ātma-para-deheṣu pradviṣantaḥ abhyasūyakāḥ ||

morph.gloss: egotism, the sense of 'I' (acc. sg. masc., object of saṃśritāḥ, first item)
force, violence (acc. sg. neut., object, second item)
pride, insolence, arrogance (acc. sg. masc., object, third item)
desire (acc. sg. masc., object, fourth item)
anger (acc. sg. masc., object, fifth item)
and

I (mām: acc. sg., object of pradviṣantaḥ; simply joined with ātmaparadeheṣu, 'me')

sentences.l: Given-over-to egotism, force, pride, desire, and anger, hating me in the bodies of self and others, malicious —
sentences.i: Given over to egotism, violence, pride, desire and anger, they hate me as I dwell in their own bodies and in others', and are malicious besides —
sentences.n: A list of five things such men are saṃśritāḥ, 'given over to' — ahaṃkāram, balam, darpam, kāmam, krodham, 'egotism, force, pride, desire, anger' — leads to the verse's real charge: mām ātma-para-deheṣu pradviṣantaḥ, 'hating me in the bodies of self and others'. The 'me' is Kṛṣṇa as the indwelling self present in every body, the same presence taught at length in chapter 13 (the kṣetrajña) and named directly at 6.29's sarva-bhūta-stham ātmānam — so that hatred directed at any being is, in the poem's logic, hatred of Kṛṣṇa himself. Abhyasūyakāḥ, 'malicious, fault-finding', closes the list.

sentences.t:
तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् ।
क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥
sentences.tr:
tān aham dviṣataḥ krūrān saṃsāreṣu nara-adhamān |
kṣipāmi ajasram aśubhān āsurīṣu eva yoniṣu ||

I (nom. sg., subject)
hating (dviṣant: present participle; dviṣataḥ: acc. pl. masc., agreeing with tān, 'hating [me]')

cruel, savage (krūrān: acc. pl. masc., agreeing with tān; the source here corrects Wikisource's misprint क्रुरान् — short u — to क्रूरान्, long ū, matching the BORI reading krūrān; the correction is adopted throughout this reading and translation)

man (first member; nara+adhamān→narādhamān, a+a→ā)

to hurl, cast down (kṣipāmi: present 1st sg., 'I hurl'; kṣipāmi+ajasram→kṣipāmyajasram, -i+a-→-y a-)

sentences.l: Those hating [me], cruel, basest-of-men — evil — I hurl, continually, in the rounds-of-rebirth, into demonic wombs alone.
sentences.i: Those hateful, cruel, and vilest of men, ever wicked, I continually hurl down, through the cycle of rebirth, into demonic wombs alone.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa now states the consequence directly, in the first person: tān aham ... kṣipāmi, 'those men I hurl down'. Krūrān, 'cruel' (agreeing with tān, 'those'), is a correction: the source text here restores क्रूरान् (long ū), correcting a Wikisource misprint क्रुरान् (short u), and matches the BORI reading krūrān; the correction is adopted throughout this reading and translation, as it must be named here per the pipeline's editorial rule. Saṃsāreṣu, 'in the rounds of rebirth', names the whole sphere across which the hurling takes place, not a single destination; āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu, 'into demonic wombs alone', with eva restrictively emphasizing that no other kind of rebirth awaits them.

sentences.t:
आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि ।
मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥
sentences.tr:
āsurīm yonim āpannāḥ mūḍhāḥ janmani janmani |
mām aprāpya eva kaunteya tataḥ yānti adhamām gatim ||

morph.gloss: demonic (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with yonim)
womb (acc. sg. fem., object of āpannāḥ; simply joined with āpannāḥ)
fallen into (āpanna: past participle; āpannāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject)
deluded, confused (mūḍha: past participle; mūḍhāḥ: nom. pl. masc., in apposition; visarga dropped before the following voiced j- of janmani, as elsewhere in this chapter)

birth (loc. sg., the word doubled to express repetition, 'birth after birth')
I (mām: acc. sg., object of aprāpya; simply joined with aprāpya, 'me')
not attaining (aprāpya: gerund; aprāpya+eva→aprāpyaiva, a+e→ai)
indeed, even, alone
son of Kuntī, Arjuna (vocative)

to go (yānti: present 3rd pl., 'they go'; yānti+adhamām→yāntyadhamām, -i+a-→-y a-)
lowest, basest (adhamām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with gatim)
course, goal, destiny (acc. sg. fem., object of yānti)

sentences.l: Fallen into a demonic womb, deluded, birth after birth, not-attaining me at all, O Kaunteya, they go, thence, to the lowest state.
sentences.i: Fallen into a demonic womb, deluded from birth to birth, never reaching me, Kaunteya, they sink at last to the lowest state.
sentences.n: This closes the long central section (verses 6-20) on the demonic nature. Janmani janmani, 'in birth, in birth', doubles a single locative to mean 'birth after birth', a common Sanskrit device for expressing repetition (compare pratyakṣam pratyakṣam and similar doublings elsewhere in the epics). Mām aprāpyaiva, 'without ever attaining me' (aprāpya+eva→aprāpyaiva, a+e→ai), states in the negative what verse 18's hatred already implied: cut off from Kṛṣṇa lifetime after lifetime, they sink, yānti, to adhamāṃ gatim, 'the lowest state' — the grim endpoint of the chapter's central portrait. Kaunteya, 'son of Kuntī', is again Arjuna.

sentences.t:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
sentences.tr:
trividham narakasya idam dvāram nāśanam ātmanaḥ |
kāmaḥ krodhaḥ tathā lobhaḥ tasmāt etat trayam tyajet ||

gate, door (nom. sg. neut., subject, in apposition with idam)

self (ātmanaḥ: gen. sg., object of nāśanam, 'destructive of the self')

anger (krodhaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject, second item; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)
likewise (adverb)

this (etat: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with trayam; tasmāt+etat→tasmādetat, -t+e-→-d e-)

sentences.l: Threefold [is] this gate of hell, destructive-of-the-self — desire, and anger, and likewise greed; therefore one-should-abandon this triad.
sentences.i: This gate of hell has three parts, and it destroys the self: desire, anger, and greed. One should therefore give up all three.
sentences.n: The chapter turns to its closing counsel (verses 21-22). Narakasya idam dvāram, 'this gate of hell' (narakasya+idam→narakasyedam, a+i→e), trividham, 'threefold', is named outright: kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhaḥ, 'desire, anger, and likewise greed' — the first two already named repeatedly through the chapter (verses 4, 8, 10, 12, 18), the third, lobha, 'greed', introduced here for the first time, completing the set. Ātmanaḥ nāśanam, 'destructive of the self', names the stakes directly: these three do not merely lead to hell, they annihilate the self that falls into them.

sentences.t:
एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः ।
आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
sentences.tr:
etaiḥ vimuktaḥ kaunteya tamaḥ-dvāraiḥ tribhiḥ naraḥ |
ācarati ātmanaḥ śreyaḥ tataḥ yāti parām gatim ||

freed, released (vimukta: past participle; vimuktaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aiḥ+v-→-air v-)
Arjuna (vocative)
darkness (first member; tamaḥ+dvāraiḥ→tamodvāraiḥ, -aḥ before d-→-o)
gate (tamo-dvāraiḥ: 'the dark gates', instr. pl., agreeing with etaiḥ, resuming verse 21's triad)
three (tribhiḥ: instr. pl.; -aiḥ+t-→-ais t-)
man (naraḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -iḥ+n-→-ir n-)
to practice, perform, do (ācarati: present 3rd sg., 'he does'; ācarati+ātmanaḥ→ācaratyātmanaḥ, -i+ā-→-y ā-)
self (ātmanaḥ: gen. sg., 'for himself')
the good, the beneficial (śreyaḥ: acc. sg. neut., object of ācarati; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)
then, thereafter (adverb; -aḥ before y-→-o)
to go (yāti: present 3rd sg., 'he goes')
highest, supreme (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with gatim)
course, goal, destiny (acc. sg. fem., object of yāti)

sentences.l: Freed from these three dark-gates, O Kaunteya, a man does what-is-good for himself; thence he goes to the highest goal.
sentences.i: A man who is freed from these three dark gates, Kaunteya, does what is best for himself, and so reaches the highest goal.
sentences.n: This answers verse 21's warning with its positive counterpart: etaiḥ ... tamo-dvāraiḥ tribhiḥ vimuktaḥ naraḥ, 'a man freed from these three dark gates' (tamo-dvāraiḥ, 'gates of darkness', renaming verse 21's triad with the word tamas, the same guṇa of darkness and inertia described at length in chapter 14), ācarati ātmanaḥ śreyaḥ, 'does what is good for himself', and so yāti parāṃ gatim, 'goes to the highest goal' — the same phrase, parāṃ gatim, that verse 23 will deny to the man who ignores scripture, and verse 20 denied, in its low form (adhamāṃ gatim), to the demonic.

sentences.t:
यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः ।
न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥
sentences.tr:
yaḥ śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya vartate kāma-kārataḥ |
na sa siddhim avāpnoti na sukham na parām gatim ||

morph.gloss: who (nom. sg. masc. relative, subject)
scripture, sacred teaching (first member)
injunction, rule (śāstra-vidhim: 'the injunction of scripture', acc. sg. masc., object of utsṛjya; simply joined with utsṛjya)
abandoning, casting aside (utsṛjya: gerund)
to act, proceed (vartate: present middle 3rd sg.)
desire (first member)
acting, doing (kāma-kāra: 'acting from mere desire, self-will', with the adverbial suffix -tas: kāma-kārataḥ, 'according to mere desire, willfully')
not
he (nom. sg. masc., subject, referring to yaḥ)
perfection, success (acc. sg. fem., object of avāpnoti; simply joined)
to attain, obtain (avāpnoti: present 3rd sg.)
not
happiness (acc. sg. neut., object)
not
highest, supreme (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with gatim)
course, goal, destiny (acc. sg. fem., object)

sentences.l: Who, having-abandoned the injunction-of-scripture, acts according-to-mere-desire — he attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the highest goal.
sentences.i: Whoever casts aside the injunctions of scripture and acts on mere desire attains neither success, nor happiness, nor the highest goal.
sentences.n: A relative-correlative sentence (yaḥ ... sa, 'who ... he') states the chapter's practical conclusion: whoever śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya, 'having abandoned the injunction of scripture', vartate kāma-kārataḥ, 'acts according to mere desire, willfully' (kāma-kāra, 'acting from desire', with the adverbial suffix -tas), na sa siddhim avāpnoti, na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim, 'attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the highest goal' — a triple negation that denies him everything the chapter has held out as the reward of the divine endowment.

sentences.t:
तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ ।
ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
sentences.tr:
tasmāt śāstram pramāṇam te kārya-akārya-vyavasthitau |
jñātvā śāstra-vidhāna-uktam karma kartum iha arhasi ||

scripture, sacred teaching (nom. sg. neut., subject)
authority, standard, measure (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
for you, your (te: enclitic dat./gen. sg.)
what is to be done, duty (gerundive of kṛ; first member)
what is not to be done (second member; kārya+akārya→kāryākārya, a+a→ā)

to know (jñātvā: gerund, 'having known')
scripture (first member)
ordinance, prescription (second member; śāstra+vidhāna→śāstravidhāna)
declared (ukta: past participle; śāstra-vidhāna-uktam: 'what is declared by the ordinance of scripture', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with karma; vidhāna+uktam→vidhānoktam, a+u→o)
action, deed (acc. sg. neut., object of kartum)
to do (kartum: infinitive, 'to do')

sentences.l: Therefore scripture [is] the authority for-you in-determining-what-should-and-should-not-be-done; having-known what-is-declared-by-the-ordinance-of-scripture, you-ought to-act here.
sentences.i: Scripture, therefore, is your authority in deciding what should and should not be done. Knowing what the ordinance of scripture declares, you should act accordingly in this world.
sentences.n: The chapter's closing verse draws the moral in general terms, anticipating the poem's own return to this same argument at 18.5-6, and its final closing counsel at 18.63-66: tasmāt śāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te, 'therefore scripture is your authority' (tasmāt+śāstram→tasmācchāstram, -t+ś-→-c ch-), kāryākāryavyavasthitau, 'in determining what should and should not be done' (kārya, 'what is to be done', and its negation a-kārya). The final construction, jñātvā ... kartum ihārhasi, 'having known ..., you ought to act here [in this world]', pairs a gerund of knowing with an infinitive-plus-'ought' of doing — knowledge of the rule is only the first step; acting on it is the point.

glossary.पार्थ: pārtha — Pārtha — son of Pṛthā, Arjuna (vocative)
glossary.संपदमासुरीम्: sampadam āsurīm — sampad — endowment, inheritance (sampadam: acc. sg. fem., result-accusative object, as at verse 3; simply joined with āsurīm); āsurī — demonic (fem. adj. of āsura; āsurīm: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with sampadam)
glossary.दैवी: daivī — daivī — divine (fem. adj., nom. sg., subject)
glossary.संपद्विमोक्षाय: sampat vimokṣāya — sampad — endowment, inheritance (sampat: nom. sg. fem., subject; sampat+vimokṣāya→sampad vimokṣāya, -t+v-→-d v-, a stop voiced before the following voiced consonant); vi-mokṣa — liberation, release (vimokṣāya: dat. sg., 'for liberation', purpose)
glossary.निबन्धायासुरी: nibandhāya āsurī — ni-bandha — bondage (nibandhāya: dat. sg., 'for bondage', purpose, paired with vimokṣāya); āsurī — demonic (fem. adj., nom. sg., subject, second of the pair; nibandhāya+āsurī→nibandhāyāsurī, a+ā→ā)
glossary.मता: matā — man — thought, held to be, considered (mata: past participle of man; matā: nom. sg. fem., predicate, agreeing with both daivī and āsurī of this verse)
glossary.मा: mā — mā — do not (prohibitive particle, taking the following injunctive)
glossary.शुचः: śucaḥ — śuc — to grieve (śucaḥ: injunctive 2nd sg. with mā, 'do not grieve')
glossary.दैवीमभिजातोऽसि: daivīm abhijātaḥ asi — daivī — divine (daivīm: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with sampadam; simply joined with abhijātaḥ); abhi-jan — born to (abhijāta: past participle; abhijātaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate agreeing with 'you'; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); as — to be (asi: present 2nd sg., 'you are')
glossary.पाण्डव: pāṇḍava — Pāṇḍava — son of Pāṇḍu, Arjuna (vocative)
glossary.द्वौ: dvau — dvi — two (dvau: nom. dual masc.)
glossary.भूतसर्गौ: bhūta-sargau — bhūta — a being, a creature (first member); sarga — creation, class, order (bhūta-sarga: 'classes of created beings', nom. dual masc., subject)
glossary.लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव: loke asmin daivaḥ — loka — world (loke: loc. sg.; loke+asmin→loke'smin, e+a→e with the a- elided, marked by avagraha); idam — this (asmin: loc. sg. masc., 'in this'); daiva — divine (daivaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, first of the pair; asmin+daivaḥ simply joined, the dental nasal unaffected before the following dental d-; daivaḥ's own visarga then drops before the following āsuraḥ, hiatus kept rather than coalescing — the same accepted epic option flagged for āsuraḥ eva immediately below, and already seen at 15.16's akṣaraḥ eva.)
glossary.आसुर: āsuraḥ — āsura — demonic (nom. sg. masc., predicate, second of the pair; -aḥ+e-→-a e-, hiatus retained rather than fusing to -aiva, as at 15.16's akṣaraḥ eva — an accepted option in epic verse)
glossary.दैवो: daivaḥ — daiva — the divine [kind] (nom. sg. masc., subject, resuming 6a's daivaḥ; -aḥ before v-→-o)
glossary.विस्तरशः: vistaraśaḥ — vistara — extension, fullness, detail (vistaraśaḥ: adverb, 'at length, in detail', formed with the adverbial suffix -śas)
glossary.प्रोक्त: proktaḥ — pra-vac — declared, described (prokta: past participle; proktaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate agreeing with daivaḥ, 'has been described'; final -ḥ dropped before the following vowel a-, hiatus retained as at 6a)
glossary.आसुरं: āsuram — āsura — the demonic [kind] (acc. sg. masc., object of śṛṇu, resuming bhūtasargau)
glossary.मे: me — aham — I (me: enclitic gen./abl. sg., 'from me')
glossary.शृणु: śṛṇu — śru — to hear (śṛṇu: imperative 2nd sg., 'hear!')
glossary.प्रवृत्तिं: pravṛttim — pravṛtti — right action, engagement, activity (acc. sg. fem., object of viduḥ)
glossary.निवृत्तिं: nivṛttim — ni-vṛt — cessation, withdrawal from action (acc. sg. fem., object of viduḥ)
glossary.जना: janāḥ — jana — a person, people (janāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; -āḥ before n-→-ā)
glossary.विदुरासुराः: viduḥ āsurāḥ — vid — to know (viduḥ: perfect 3rd pl. used as present, 'they know'; -uḥ+ā-→-ur ā-, the visarga after u becoming r before a voiced sound); āsura — demonic (āsurāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject, in apposition with janāḥ, 'demonic people')
glossary.शौचं: śaucam — śauca — purity, cleanliness (nom. sg. neut., subject)
glossary.नापि: na api — na — not (na+api→nāpi, a+a→ā); api — also, even
glossary.चाचारो: ca ācāraḥ — ca — and (ca+ācāraḥ→cācāraḥ, a+ā→ā); ā-car — right conduct, proper behavior (ācāraḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before n-→-o)
glossary.सत्यं: satyam — satya — truth, truthfulness (nom. sg. neut., subject)
glossary.तेषु: teṣu — tad — in them (teṣu: loc. pl. masc., referring to the āsurāḥ of the first line)
glossary.विद्यते: vidyate — vid — to exist, be found (vidyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is found')
glossary.असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं: asatyam apratiṣṭham — a-satya — unreal, untrue (asatyam: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with jagat, first predicate; simply joined with apratiṣṭham); a-pratiṣṭha — without foundation, groundless (apratiṣṭham: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with jagat, second predicate)
glossary.ते: te — tad — they (te: nom. pl. masc., subject, referring to the āsurāḥ of verse 7)
glossary.जगदाहुरनीश्वरम्: jagat āhuḥ anīśvaram — jagat — the world (acc. sg. neut., object of āhuḥ; jagat+āhuḥ→jagadāhuḥ, -t+ā-→-d ā-, a stop voiced before a vowel); ā-ah — to say, declare (āhuḥ: perfect 3rd pl., 'they say'; -uḥ+a-→-ur a-, the visarga after u becoming r before a voiced sound); an-īśvara — without a lord, without a god, godless (anīśvaram: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with jagat, third predicate)
glossary.अपरस्परसंभूतं: aparaspara-saṃbhūtam — aparaspara — one another, mutual(ly) (an old form synonymous with the more familiar paraspara, so glossed already by Śaṅkara — not the privative a- 'not', which would reverse the sense; first member); sam-bhū — produced, arisen (saṃbhūta: past participle; aparaspara-saṃbhūtam: 'produced by mutual union', acc. sg. neut., predicate agreeing with jagat)
glossary.किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम्: kim anyat kāma-haitukam — kim — what? (interrogative, 'what else [could it be]'); anya — other, else (nom./acc. sg. neut.); kāma — desire (first member); haituka — caused by, having as its cause (from hetu, 'cause'; kāma-haitukam: 'caused by desire alone', acc. sg. neut., predicate)
glossary.एतां: etām — etad — this (etām: acc. sg. fem., object of avaṣṭabhya, 'this view')
glossary.दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य: dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya — dṛṣṭi — a view, an opinion, an outlook (acc. sg. fem., object of avaṣṭabhya; simply joined with avaṣṭabhya); ava-stambh — to hold fast to, cling to, adopt (avaṣṭabhya: gerund, 'having taken hold of')
glossary.नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः: naṣṭa-ātmānaḥ alpa-buddhayaḥ — naṣṭa — lost, ruined (past participle of naś; first member); ātman — self (naṣṭa-ātman: 'whose self is lost', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); alpa — little, small (first member); buddhi — intelligence, understanding (alpa-buddhi: 'of little intelligence', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., in apposition)
glossary.प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः: prabhavanti ugra-karmāṇaḥ — pra-bhū — to arise, come forth (prabhavanti: present 3rd pl., 'they arise'; -i+u-→-y u-); ugra — fierce, terrible (first member); karman — deed, action (ugra-karman: 'of fierce deeds', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., in apposition)
glossary.क्षयाय: kṣayāya — kṣaya — destruction, ruin (dat. sg., purpose; jagataḥ below serves both kṣayāya and ahitāḥ, 'for the destruction of the world' and 'enemies of the world')
glossary.जगतोऽहिताः: jagataḥ ahitāḥ — jagat — world (jagataḥ: gen. sg.; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); a-hita — hostile, harmful (ahitāḥ: nom. pl. masc., predicate, 'as enemies')
glossary.काममाश्रित्य: kāmam āśritya — kāma — desire (acc. sg. masc., object of āśritya; simply joined with āśritya); ā-śri — to resort to, give oneself over to (āśritya: gerund, 'having given themselves over to')
glossary.दुष्पूरं: duṣpūram — duṣ-pūra — hard to fill, insatiable (duṣ- 'ill, hard' + pūra 'filling'; acc. sg. masc., agreeing with kāmam)
glossary.दम्भमानमदान्विताः: dambha-māna-mada-anvitāḥ — dambha — hypocrisy, deceit, ostentation (first member); māna — pride, self-conceit (second member); mada — arrogance (third member); anvita — possessed by, filled with (from anu-i; dambha-māna-mada-anvitāḥ: 'filled with hypocrisy, pride and arrogance', nom. pl. masc., subject)
glossary.मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुच: mohāt gṛhītvā asat-grāhān pravartante aśuci-vratāḥ — moha — delusion (mohāt: abl. sg., 'through delusion'; mohāt+gṛhītvā→mohādgṛhītvā, -t+g-→-d g-); grah — to seize, adopt (gṛhītvā: gerund, 'having adopted'; gṛhītvā+asadgrāhān→gṛhītvāsadgrāhān, ā+a→ā); a-sat — untrue, false (first member); grāha — a notion, a tenet, a holding (asat-grāha: 'false notions', acc. pl. masc., object of gṛhītvā; -t+g-→-d g-); pra-vṛt — to proceed, act (pravartante: present middle 3rd pl., 'they act'; grāhān+pravartante simply joined, the final -n unaffected before p-); a-śuci — impure (first member); vrata — a vow, a resolve, an observance (aśuci-vratāḥ: 'whose resolves are impure', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject; pravartante+aśucivratāḥ→pravartante'śucivratāḥ, -e+a-→-e' with avagraha) — the densest single-token sandhi run in this chapter: the whole second half-line is one written token
glossary.चिन्तामपरिमेयां: cintām aparimeyām — cintā — anxiety, care, worry (acc. sg. fem., object of upāśritāḥ; simply joined with aparimeyām); a-parimeya — immeasurable, unlimited (aparimeyām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with cintām)
glossary.प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः: pralaya-antām upāśritāḥ — pra-laya — dissolution, death (first member; pralaya+antām→pralayāntām, a+a→ā); anta — end (pralaya-antām: 'ending [only] in death', acc. sg. fem., agreeing with cintām; simply joined with upāśritāḥ); upa-ā-śri — beset by, given over to (upāśrita: past participle; upāśritāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject)
glossary.कामोपभोगपरमा: kāma-upabhoga-paramāḥ — kāma — desire (first member); upa-bhoga — enjoyment (second member; kāma+upabhoga→kāmopabhoga, a+u→o); parama — highest, supreme (kāma-upabhoga-paramāḥ: 'holding sense-enjoyment as the highest goal', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject; its own -āḥ drops before the following vowel of etāvat, as elsewhere in this chapter wherever a plural in -āḥ meets a voiced sound.)
glossary.एतावदिति: etāvat iti — etāvat — this much, so much (nom. sg. neut., 'this is all [there is]'); iti — thus, [thinking] (quotation particle marking the preceding as a thought; etāvat+iti→etāvaditi, -t+i-→-d i-, a stop voiced before a vowel)
glossary.निश्चिताः: niścitāḥ — ni-ci — determined, certain, resolved (niścita: past participle; niścitāḥ: nom. pl. masc., predicate agreeing with the subject)
glossary.आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः: āśā-pāśa-śataiḥ baddhāḥ — āśā — hope, expectation (first member); pāśa — a tie, a bond, a snare (second member; āśā+pāśa→āśāpāśa); śata — a hundred (āśā-pāśa-śataiḥ: 'by hundreds of ties of hope', instr. pl.; -aiḥ+b-→-air b-); bandh — bound, tied (baddha: past participle; baddhāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject, 'bound')
glossary.कामक्रोधपरायणाः: kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ — kāma — desire (first member); krodha — anger (second member); parāyaṇa — intent on, given over to (kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ: 'given over to desire and anger', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., in apposition)
glossary.ईहन्ते: īhante — īh — to strive, endeavor (īhante: present middle 3rd pl., 'they strive')
glossary.कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान्: kāma-bhoga-artham anyāyena artha-sañcayān — kāma — desire (first member); bhoga — enjoyment (second member; kāma+bhoga→kāmabhoga); artha — purpose, sake (kāma-bhoga-artham: 'for the sake of gratifying desire', adverbial acc.; simply joined with anyāyena); a-nyāya — injustice, wrong means (anyāyena: instr. sg., 'by unjust means'; anyāyena+arthasañcayān→anyāyenārthasañcayān, a+a→ā); artha — wealth, riches (first member); sañcaya — accumulation, amassing (artha-sañcayān: 'hoards of wealth', acc. pl. masc., object of īhante)
glossary.इदमद्य: idam adya — idam — this (nom./acc. sg. neut., understood object, 'this [much]'); adya — today, now (adverb)
glossary.मया: mayā — aham — I (mayā: instr. sg., 'by me')
glossary.लब्धमिमं: labdham imam — labh — obtained, gained (labdha: past participle; labdham: nom. sg. neut., predicate, 'this has been gained'); idam — this (imam: acc. sg. masc., object of prāpsye, vulgate reading agreeing with manoratham, masc.; BORI reads idam, neuter, in its place — see the note)
glossary.प्राप्स्ये: prāpsye — pra-āp — to reach, attain, obtain (prāpsye: future middle 1st sg., 'I shall gain')
glossary.मनोरथम्: manoratham — manas — mind (first member); ratha — chariot; manoratha 'mind's chariot', i.e. a wish, a desire (acc. sg. masc., object of prāpsye)
glossary.इदमस्तीदमपि: idam asti idam api — idam — this (nom. sg. neut., subject, 'this is [mine]'); as — to be (asti: present 3rd sg., 'is'; asti+idam→astīdam, i+i→ī); idam — this (nom. sg. neut., subject, second clause; simply joined with api); api — also, too
glossary.भविष्यति: bhaviṣyati — bhū — to be, become (bhaviṣyati: future 3rd sg., 'will be')
glossary.पुनर्धनम्: punaḥ dhanam — punar — again, further (punar: adverb; the basic form of this word before voiced sounds, with punaḥ its pausa form; punaḥ+dhanam→punardhanam); dhana — wealth (nom. sg. neut., subject, 'this wealth too [shall be mine]')
glossary.असौ: asau — adas — that (asau: nom. sg. masc., subject, 'that [enemy]')
glossary.हतः: hataḥ — han — slain (hata: past participle; hataḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, 'has been slain')
glossary.शत्रुर्हनिष्ये: śatruḥ haniṣye — śatru — enemy (śatruḥ: nom. sg. masc., in apposition with asau; -uḥ+h-→-ur h-); han — to slay (haniṣye: future middle 1st sg., 'I shall slay')
glossary.चापरानपि: ca aparān api — ca — and (ca+aparān→cāparān, a+a→ā); a-para — other (aparān: acc. pl. masc., object of haniṣye; simply joined with api); api — also, too
glossary.ईश्वरोऽहमहं: īśvaraḥ aham aham — īśvara — lord, master, ruler (nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); aham — I (nom. sg., subject, 'I am the lord'); aham — I (nom. sg., subject, repeated for the next clause; simply joined with bhogī)
glossary.भोगी: bhogī — bhogin — enjoyer, one who enjoys (nom. sg. masc., predicate, 'I am the enjoyer')
glossary.सिद्धोऽहं: siddhaḥ aham — sidh — accomplished, perfected (siddha: past participle; siddhaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); aham — I (nom. sg., subject, repeated a third time)
glossary.बलवान्सुखी: balavān sukhī — balavat — powerful, strong (balavān: nom. sg. masc., predicate); sukhin — happy (nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि: āḍhyaḥ abhijanavān asmi — āḍhya — wealthy, rich (nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); abhijanavat — well-born, of good lineage (abhijanavān: nom. sg. masc., predicate; simply joined with asmi); as — to be (asmi: present 1st sg., 'I am')
glossary.कोऽन्योऽस्ति: kaḥ anyaḥ asti — kim — who? (kaḥ: nom. sg. masc. interrogative; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); anya — other, else (anyaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); as — to be, to exist (asti: present 3rd sg., 'is there')
glossary.सदृशो: sadṛśaḥ — sa-dṛśa — like, equal to (sadṛśaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate agreeing with anyaḥ; -aḥ before m-→-o)
glossary.यक्ष्ये: yakṣye — yaj — to sacrifice (yakṣye: future middle 1st sg., 'I shall sacrifice' — the ātmanepada 'for oneself' form)
glossary.दास्यामि: dāsyāmi — dā — to give (dāsyāmi: future 1st sg., 'I shall give')
glossary.मोदिष्य: modiṣye — mud — to rejoice (modiṣye: future middle 1st sg., 'I shall rejoice'; before the following iti its ātmanepada -e ending drops to -a rather than the usual hiatus or coalescence — an idiosyncratic sandhi of this ending before iti, attested here in the transmitted text: modiṣye+iti→modiṣya iti)
glossary.इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः: iti ajñāna-vimohitāḥ — iti — thus, [so they think] (quotation particle, closing the interior monologue begun at verse 13; iti+ajñāna→ityajñāna, -i+a-→-y a-); a-jñāna — ignorance (first member); vi-muh — deluded (vimohita: past participle, causative; vimohitāḥ: nom. pl. masc., predicate, the narrator's own judgment on the men just quoted)
glossary.अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता: aneka-citta-vibhrāntāḥ — an-eka — not one, manifold, many (first member); citta — thought, mind (second member; aneka+citta→anekacitta); vi-bhram — bewildered, distracted (vibhrānta: past participle; aneka-citta-vibhrāntāḥ: 'bewildered by manifold thoughts', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject)
glossary.मोहजालसमावृताः: moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ — moha — delusion (first member); jāla — a net, a web (moha-jāla: 'the net of delusion', second member); sam-ā-vṛ — enveloped, entangled (samāvṛta: past participle; moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ: 'entangled in the net of delusion', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., in apposition)
glossary.प्रसक्ताः: prasaktāḥ — pra-sañj — attached to, addicted to (prasakta: past participle; prasaktāḥ: nom. pl. masc., predicate)
glossary.कामभोगेषु: kāma-bhogeṣu — kāma — desire (first member); bhoga — enjoyment (kāma-bhogeṣu: 'in the gratification of desire', loc. pl.)
glossary.पतन्ति: patanti — pat — to fall (patanti: present 3rd pl., 'they fall')
glossary.नरकेऽशुचौ: narake aśucau — naraka — hell (loc. sg., 'into hell'); a-śuci — foul, impure (aśucau: loc. sg., agreeing with narake; -e+a-→-e' with avagraha)
glossary.आत्मसंभाविताः: ātma-saṃbhāvitāḥ — ātman — self (first member); sam-bhū — esteemed, self-conceited (causative saṃbhāvita, 'considered, esteemed'; ātma-saṃbhāvitāḥ: 'self-conceited', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject)
glossary.स्तब्धा: stabdhāḥ — stambh — stiff, obstinate, arrogant (stabdha: past participle; stabdhāḥ: nom. pl. masc., in apposition; the visarga of -āḥ drops before the following voiced dh- of dhanamānamadānvitāḥ, as elsewhere in this chapter wherever a plural in -āḥ meets a voiced sound)
glossary.धनमानमदान्विताः: dhana-māna-mada-anvitāḥ — dhana — wealth (first member); māna — pride, self-conceit (second member); mada — arrogance (third member; dhana+māna+mada→dhanamānamada); anvita — filled with, possessed by (dhana-māna-mada-anvitāḥ: 'filled with the pride and arrogance of wealth', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., in apposition; dhanamānamada+anvitāḥ→dhanamānamadānvitāḥ, a+a→ā)
glossary.यजन्ते: yajante — yaj — to sacrifice (yajante: present middle 3rd pl., 'they sacrifice')
glossary.नामयज्ञैस्ते: nāma-yajñaiḥ te — nāman — name (first member); yajña — sacrifice (nāma-yajñaiḥ: 'with sacrifices that are such in name only', instr. pl.); tad — they (te: nom. pl. masc., subject, resuming verse 17a; -aiḥ+t-→-ais t-)

about: Chapter 16, Daivāsurasampadvibhāgayoga, the Yoga of the Division between the Divine and Demonic Endowments, continues without any question from Arjuna, moving from chapter 15's vision of the Supreme Person to a stark moral portrait of two kinds of created beings. Kṛṣṇa opens with two matching catalogs: the divine endowment (daivī sampad) — fearlessness, purity of being, self-control, non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, compassion, gentleness, patience, and more — and, set directly against it, the demonic endowment (āsurī sampad) — hypocrisy, pride, self-conceit, anger, harshness, ignorance. The one leads to liberation, the other to bondage, and Kṛṣṇa reassures Arjuna that he himself was born with the divine nature. The chapter then turns, at length, to portray the demonic mind from the inside: those who hold the world to be godless and without foundation, produced by nothing but the chance union of male and female and driven by desire alone; who chase insatiable appetite, hoard wealth by unjust means, and rehearse to themselves a boastful inner monologue — "this I have gained, this I shall gain next, I am the lord, I am accomplished, who is there like me?" — even as they perform sacrifice only in name, out of hypocrisy and without regard for scriptural rule, and hate the divine presence in their own bodies and in others'. Such men, Kṛṣṇa says, he hurls again and again into demonic wombs, sinking further from him birth after birth. The chapter closes by naming the threefold gate of hell that destroys the self — desire, anger, and greed — urging their abandonment, and ends with a plain statement of the poem's governing principle: whoever discards the authority of scripture and acts on mere desire attains neither success, nor happiness, nor the highest goal, so that scripture must be the standard by which one determines what should and should not be done.
